pyro.name: Pyro Ward
notes: ▸ **Hydro** is the fastest way to remove this ward, as every 1U of Hydro removes 2U of Pyro.
▸ Secondly, **Electro** is also okay, removing 1U of Pyro for every 1U of Electro.

hydro.name: Hydro Ward
notes: ▸ **Dendro** is the fastest way to remove this ward, as every 1U of Dendro removes 2U of Hydro.
▸ Secondly, **Cryo** is also okay, removing 1U of Hydro for every 1U of Cryo.
▸ Alternatively, **Electro** also works well, as it has a 0.4U per second DoT, which, while usually worse, can outperform teams that struggle to consistently apply Cryo, or rarely, Dendro.

electro.name: Electro Ward
notes: ▸ For this ward, **Pyro**, **Cryo** and **Dendro** all remove the same 1U of Electro for every 1U of their element.
▸ Alternatively, **Hydro** also works well, as it has a 0.4U per second DoT, which, while usually worse, can outperform teams that struggle to consistently apply Pyro, Cryo or Dendro.
▸ Since Electro wards have no reaction that removes more than 1U of Electro per 1U applied, they are theoretically more difficult to break than Hydro wards, which makes Hydro a better alternative.

cryo.name: Cryo Ward
notes: ▸ **Pyro** is the fastest way to remove this ward, as every 1U of Pyro removes 2U of Cryo.
▸ Secondly, **Electro** is also okay, removing 1U of Cryo for every 1U of Electro.

dendro.name: Dendro Ward
notes: ▸ **Electro** is the best direct counter to remove this ward, as every 1U of Electro removes 1U of Dendro.
▸ However, **Pyro** (Burning) can sometimes outperform Electro, if the team struggles to apply Electro consistently.
▸ Alternatively, **Hydro** is the next best direct counter, as it's the only element left that removes any Dendro ward durability, with Hydro removing 0.5U of Dendro for every 1U of Hydro.

geo.name: Geo Ward
notes: ▸ For Geo wards, the most effective way to remove one is to use **Blunt** attacks and **Geo** characters. Blunt attacks include: **Claymore attacks**, most **Plunge attacks**, **Geo attacks**, **Overload** explosions
▸ Due to Geo wards having a slightly different mechanic, applying a PHEC (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, Cryo) element alone will **not** remove any durability.
▸ In order to remove durability with a PHEC element, you must first apply the element, and then apply **Geo**, in order to trigger **Crystallize**.
▸ If an enemy has a permanent Geo aura, you **cannot** reduce durability by just applying a PHEC element.
▸ The reaction itself is the one that consumes durability, and the amount is based on the remaining **aura** at the time of triggering Crystallize.
▸ Example: `Applied 2U of Pyro → 1 second passes → Applied Geo → Crystallize occurs`, will **not** consume 2U due to elemental aura decay rate.
▸ For more info on how decay rate works, do `/theory theory:elemental gauge theory section:aura decay rate`

elementless.name: Elementless Ward
notes: aaaaa

void.name: Void Ward
notes: ▸ **Void** wards are unique, as all elemental attacks consume their durability equally.
▸ However, while all elemental attacks consume durability equally, **Nightsoul**-aligned attacks are **3 times** more efficient.
▸ Nightsoul-aligned attacks are attacks from **Natlan** characters, **while being inside the Nightsoul's Blessing State**.
▸ As the second-best option after any Nightsoul-aligned attack, **Burning** is a great choice, as every **tick** of Burning damages the ward.

deepdark.name: Deepdark Ward
notes: ▸ **Deepdark** wards are unique, as they scale based off the enemy's **Max HP**.
▸ The ward takes equal amounts of damage from every type of elemental attack, however **Lunar Reaction** damage is multiplied by 300%.
▸ Lunar Reaction damage is the easiest way to break this ward, due to the multiplier it provides, however this ward isn't a check and can be broken by any character, as it only requires damage.
